comment: What the classic's FIRMWARE costs: the shipped image (esp32,server,float-f32 — lp-fw/fw-esp32v3's own default feature set, the bytes the DOM-Z-102 is flashed with) direct-loaded on lp-emu:esp32v3:t1 and read from its FIRST heartbeat triple. ⚠️ That triple is ELICITED, not idle-emitted: `esp32_memory_stats` runs on a project load/unload/stop-all or a client `runtime_status`, never on the five-second server heartbeat, so a classic boot with nobody talking prints no `[MEM]` line at all. Since wire proto 32 (plan classic-uart-on-lp-link) the classic's UART0 is an lp-link and the triple is log records on its log channel, so the gate boots through `lp-cli emu run --chip esp32v3 --host-link --json-replies`, asks with one `stopAllProjects` over the link once the hello arrives (the same request lp-cli/tests/emu_v3_link_gates.rs sends; before proto 32 it was lp-emu/lp-emu-validate/walks/v3-stop-all.script's `M!` bytes on `[INIT] I/O task spawned` +1 ms), and stops on the first `[JIT] used=` line. `--json-replies`: no learned table, so the figure is the link's cost alone. `measured` is this tree, and is the ratchet. Regenerate with `just heap-budget-baseline-chips-v3`; see docs/heap-budget-gate.md, "The second source".
sample: the FIRST heartbeat triple, elicited by one `stopAllProjects` sent over the hosted UART0 link once the board's hello arrives (~0.12 s), the run ending on the first `[JIT] used=`. Before wire proto 32: the same request as `M!` bytes on `[INIT] I/O task spawned` +1 ms, ending at 119,041 us
stack_band_note: RE-BASELINED ON ONE HOST by plan classic-uart-on-lp-link P5, 2026-09-29, on this desk (M2 Max, aarch64-apple-darwin): stackHighWater 16,600 B and usedBytes 23,944 B, against 12,744 B and 16,636 B before it. The classic's UART0 went onto lp-link (P2): the link at rest (its fixed buffers, allocated in Link::new) is most of the +7,308 B of `usedBytes`; the +3,856 B of high-water is NOT the link: the deepest point is still the boot, `boot_firmware` -> `default_esp32v3_hardware_manifest` -> `HardwareManifestFile::read_json` -> serde_json -> the allocator, with the 1 ms pacer's level-1 ISR and the swi2 io_task poll nested on it, the same chain on both images with every frame below `boot_firmware` equal. What moved is under it: the embassy main task's poll frame grew 992 -> 4,528 B (+3,536; `run_server_loop`'s future, a separate 3,584 B frame polled only after the boot, is now inlined into the main task's poll, so its locals sit under the whole boot), `boot_firmware`'s own frame +128 B, and the pacer's ISR landing 272 B deeper on that chain while io_task's poll frame shrank 320 -> 208 B (-80 net in the tail). Sampled on lp-emu:esp32v3:t1 at quantum 16, both images (origin/main ca0b3dbd9 and this branch). The runner's figure for the new image does not exist yet; the band is the measurement ±500 B rounded outward (the C6's rule). HISTORY: the BLE plan's M3 (access core), 2026-09-23, re-baselined 16,060 B / 17,044 B down to 12,732 B / 16,636 B on this desk; M5 P6 measured the pre-M3 image on TWO hosts (this desk and the `Emulator ESP32v3 (x64)` runner) and they agreed to the byte at 16,060 B / 17,044 B — see `host_band` below, which is that run's record and still describes the pre-M3 image.

silicon_reference.gap_note: largestFreeBlock, totalBytes and stackTotal are EQUAL to the byte (108526 / 241552 / 45280). usedBytes is 1,156 B lower here and stackHighWater 912 B lower, and NEITHER number is attributable yet: two confounders sit on top of them. (1) The silicon capture is a SECOND boot of a flash-backed lpfs (espflash hard-resets after writing); this run direct-loads with no flash chip at all and the firmware falls back to the memory FS, which is a different allocator load. (2) It is a different build — c976f17a9 in a cold worktree, sha256 670b7bf1…, against this tree's 22ef9067… at the same 2,985,952 bytes. The same-image, same-flash comparison is M5 P6's emulated twin, and E2's pinned +84 B `[MEM] used` claim is a statement about THAT comparison, not about these two rows.
silicon_reference.not_a_gate: A different image at a different commit on a different boot shape. Read it as the two rows it is, and gate on `measured`.

host_band.comment: The BETWEEN-HOST figure (M5 P6; DD24 R6 / DD45's shape). `build-reference-image.sh --verify` already proves ONE host's reproducibility — two cold worktrees, two paths, one sha256. This is the other question: does the same commit give the same image, and the same memory figures, on two DIFFERENT hosts? The answer on the classic is no to the first and yes to the second, which is the C6's answer too (docs/reports/2026-09-08-esp32c6-emulator-walk.md §7.2: ~4.7 KB of drift from the rustc binary's own host build; memory-class figures survive it, layout-dependent figures do not).

hosts.source: scripts/emu/build-reference-image.sh --chip esp32 esp32,server,float-f32 111976fc0 none, and `just heap-budget-check-chips-v3` in the same tree, 2026-09-11

run 34655730090, job `Emulator ESP32v3 (x64)` (103447610351) on main at 111976fc0: `build-reference-image: sha256 56abdef0…` and `file size 2986452` from the gate step, the two memory figures from the `Heap budget ratchet` step

host_band.finding:
The two ELFs DIFFER: 500 bytes, 0.017 %, at the same commit with the same Xtensa toolchain (espup 1.95.0.0) and the same host rustc version (1.97.0-nightly ca9a134e0, LLVM 22.1.2). What differs is the host triple the compiler binary itself was built for, which is the C6's §7.2 attribution and the debt note it cites. P5's own `stack_band_note` predicted 'the same 2,985,952 bytes as this host's and a different sha256'; the size half of that is CORRECTED here — it is not the same size.

And the figures the gate reads are IDENTICAL on both hosts, byte for byte: stackHighWater 16,060, usedBytes 17,044, and (from the same runs) freeBytes 224,508, largestFreeBlock 108,526, totalBytes 241,552, stackTotal 45,280. That is the finding, and it is the classic's version of 'memory-class figures survive the drift'. It is not a licence to drop the band: nothing here makes 500 B of layout drift SAFE, it only shows that this particular 500 B did not move the deepest point of the main stack.
host_band.not_a_gate: Nothing is gated on these two rows. They are the band's evidence, and the walk record's §7.2 quotes them.
